body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「一個預測模型表現不穩定，你會先試新架構、加 feature，還是先問 label 怎樣定義？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「先加多些 label，資料多了模型自然會準。」

## Label 其實是歷史過程留下的痕跡

Label 不是自然界已寫好的答案，而是某個人、系統或流程在某個時間點記下的結果。假設一個虛構的支援工作流想預測「哪份 request 需要資深 reviewer」。這個 label 可以代表後來真的被升級、首次閱讀時看起來複雜、超過某段處理時間，或被錯誤地分派。四個版本會訓練出四個不同模型，也會鼓勵四種不同的行為。若未說清楚，就算 validation score 高，也不知道模型替甚麼歷史習慣複製得最好。

還要加 observation cutoff。對 3 月 1 日收到的 request，你只能使用當日或之前已知的欄位；而「其後七日被升級」要等到 3 月 8 日才完整觀察到。把 3 月 7 日才補上的處理備註放入 3 月 1 日的 feature，是把答案偷放進題目。Label delay、缺失 label、重新開案和不同 reviewer 的標準，都應該成為資料設計的一部分。

## 畫邊個圈，決定你標記邊個

想像老師要標記「需要額外幫忙的學生」。用考試不及格、上堂舉手、最後有沒有補習，會圈出不同一群人。不是哪個圈必然錯，而是你必須先說清楚你想幫的是哪一種情況；否則你是在訓練一個猜老師舊做法的機器。

## 答題時要交代嘅判斷

先寫 decision：模型輸出只會排序讓 reviewer 先看，還是會改變處理路徑？再把正例、負例、未知例和不能用作 label 的資料寫成可審閱規則。對歷史流程有偏差或不一致的地方，不要假裝 label 是真相；把它叫作 proxy，抽樣由人檢查，並記錄不同定義帶來的差異。模型問題有時是 label contract 問題，不是模型容量問題。

## 答案何時會太薄

「用所有歷史結果做 binary label」聽起來有效率，卻可能把延遲、人工習慣和後續處理資訊混在一起。更小的 baseline 是用明確 triage checklist，由人為一小組 synthetic case 標三個狀態：可先看、一般、資訊不足。若團隊連這三類也無法一致說明，就不應急著訓練分類器。

## 技術證據

Portfolio 可以放 `label-policy.md`，內有正例／負例／unknown 的定義、observation cutoff 圖、欄位 availability 表和 history rewrite 的處理方法；再附 `label-audit.csv`、兩位 reviewer 對少量 fixture 的差異、time-safe split manifest、資料 schema test 和一個拒絕使用未來欄位的單元測試。用 `data-card.md` 記錄來源、抽樣日期、不能代表甚麼，以及為何不能推斷真實人群。

## 交付、業務與風險證據

另把流程寫成「只支援 reviewer 排序，不作自動拒絕或優先處分」。說清楚誰擁有 label 定義、標準改變時誰批准重標、何時停用排序，以及如何讓 reviewer 指出錯誤分類。不要把歷史處理結果誤稱為客觀需要或真實商業影響；它只是一個需要被檢查的過去流程訊號。

## 延伸閱讀

[Model score 要怎樣連回 workflow decision](/zh-HK/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision)、[由 offline evaluation 走到獲授權 pilot](/zh-HK/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot) 和 [由模糊需求到可驗收 feature](/zh-HK/articles/from-vague-request-to-accepted-feature)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。request、label、reviewer、資料和 artefact 全部是虛構教學草稿；不使用真實個人資料，不描述任何真實機構或客戶，也不聲稱預測帶來成果。

body.zh-Hans:
> 面试官问：“一个预测模型表现不稳定，你会先试新架构、加 feature，还是先问 label 怎样定义？”
>
> 答对一半的答案：“先加更多 label，数据多了模型自然会准。”

## Label 其实是历史流程留下的痕迹

Label 不是自然界已经写好的答案，而是某个人、系统或流程在某个时间点记录的结果。假设一个虚构的支持流程想预测“哪份 request 需要资深 reviewer”。这个 label 可以代表后来真的被升级、第一次阅读时看起来复杂、超过某段处理时间，或被错误分派。四个版本会训练出四个不同模型，也会鼓励四种不同的行为。若没有说清楚，即使 validation score 很高，也不知道模型最会复制的是哪一种历史习惯。

还要加 observation cutoff。对 3 月 1 日收到的 request，你只能使用当天或之前已知的字段；而“后来七天内被升级”要等到 3 月 8 日才完整观察到。把 3 月 7 日才补上的处理备注放进 3 月 1 日的 feature，就是把答案偷放进题目。Label delay、缺失 label、重新开案和不同 reviewer 的标准，都应成为数据设计的一部分。

## 画哪个圈，决定你标记谁

想象老师要标记“需要额外帮助的学生”。用考试不及格、上课举手、最后有没有补习，会圈出不同一群人。不是哪个圈一定错，而是你必须先说清楚想帮的是哪种情况；否则你训练的是一台猜老师旧做法的机器。

## 面试真正想听到的判断

先写 decision：模型输出只会排序让 reviewer 先看，还是会改变处理路径？接着把正例、负例、未知例和不能用作 label 的数据写成可审阅规则。对历史流程的偏差或不一致，不要假装 label 是真相；称它为 proxy，抽样交给人检查，并记录不同定义带来的差异。模型问题有时是 label contract 问题，不是模型容量问题。

## 答案什么时候太薄

“用所有历史结果做 binary label”听起来有效率，却可能把延迟、人工习惯和后续处理信息混在一起。更小的 baseline 是用清楚 triage checklist，让人为一小组 synthetic case 标三种状态：可先看、一般、信息不足。若团队连这三类也无法一致说明，就不该急着训练分类器。

## 技术证据

Portfolio 可放 `label-policy.md`，内有正例／负例／unknown 的定义、observation cutoff 图、字段 availability 表与 history rewrite 的处理方法；再附 `label-audit.csv`、两位 reviewer 对少量 fixture 的差异、time-safe split manifest、数据 schema test，以及拒绝使用未来字段的单元测试。用 `data-card.md` 记录来源、抽样日期、不能代表什么，以及为什么不能推论真实人群。

## 交付、业务与风险证据

另把流程写成“只支持 reviewer 排序，不做自动拒绝或优先处分”。说清楚谁拥有 label 定义、标准改变时谁核准重标、何时停用排序，以及 reviewer 如何标示错误分类。不要把历史处理结果误称为客观需要或真实商业影响；它只是需要检查的过去流程信号。

## 延伸阅读

[Model score 怎样连回 workflow decision](/zh-Hans/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision)、[从 offline evaluation 走到获授权 pilot](/zh-Hans/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot) 和 [从模糊需求到可验收 feature](/zh-Hans/articles/from-vague-request-to-accepted-feature)。

## 范围说明

这是 AI.DOG 的单题练习。request、label、reviewer、数据和 artefact 全是虚构教学草稿；不使用真实个人数据，不描述任何真实机构或客户，也不声称预测带来成果。
body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “A prediction model is unstable. Do you try a new architecture, add features, or first ask how the label is defined?”
>
> Half-right answer: “Add more labels. More data will naturally make the model accurate.”

## A label is a trace of a historical process

A label is not an answer written into nature. It is the result recorded by a person, system, or process at a particular time. Imagine a fictional support workflow that wants to predict which request needs a senior reviewer. The label might mean it was later escalated, it looked complex on first read, it took longer than a chosen duration, or it was assigned incorrectly. Those four definitions train four different models and encourage four different behaviours. Without a definition, even a high validation score cannot tell you which historical habit the model learned to reproduce.

Add an observation cutoff. For a request received on 1 March, use only fields known on or before 1 March. A label such as “escalated within seven days” becomes fully observable only on 8 March. Adding a note written on 7 March as a 1 March feature puts the answer inside the question. Label delay, missing labels, reopened cases, and inconsistent reviewer standards belong in the data design.

## The circle you draw determines who receives the label

Imagine a teacher marking students who need extra help. Exam failure, raising a hand in class, and eventually attending tutoring identify different groups. No circle is automatically wrong. You must say which situation you intend to support. Otherwise, you are training a machine to guess the teacher's old habits.

## The judgement an interviewer is listening for

Write the decision first: does the output only rank items for a reviewer to see, or does it change a processing path? Then define positive, negative, unknown, and disallowed label evidence as reviewable rules. Where history is biased or inconsistent, do not call the label ground truth. Call it a proxy, sample it for human checking, and record how alternate definitions change the result. What appears to be a model-capacity problem can be a label-contract problem.

## Where an answer goes thin

“Use every historical outcome as a binary label” sounds efficient, but can blend delays, staff habits, and later information into one target. A smaller baseline is a clear triage checklist where a person assigns a small set of synthetic cases to three states: review first, ordinary, or insufficient information. If the team cannot describe those three states consistently, it is too early to train a classifier.

## Technical evidence

A portfolio can include `label-policy.md` with positive, negative, and unknown rules, an observation-cutoff diagram, a field-availability table, and a treatment for rewritten history. Add `label-audit.csv`, two reviewers' differences on a small fixture, a time-safe split manifest, a schema test, and a unit test that rejects future fields. A `data-card.md` should state the source, sampling date, representational limits, and why it cannot support claims about a real population.

## Delivery, business, and risk evidence

Write the workflow as “reviewer ranking support only, with no automatic rejection or priority decision.” State who owns the label definition, who approves relabelling when standards change, when ranking is disabled, and how a reviewer can flag a wrong classification. Do not turn a historical process outcome into an objective need or a business-impact claim. It is a past workflow signal that must be examined.

## Further reading

[Connect a model score to a workflow decision](/en/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision), [move from offline evaluation to an authorised pilot](/en/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot), and [turn a vague request into an accepted feature](/en/articles/from-vague-request-to-accepted-feature).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Requests, labels, reviewers, data, and artefacts are fictional teaching-draft material. It uses no real personal data, describes no real organisation or customer, and makes no claim that a prediction produced an outcome.
